title: Biochar amendment and soil moisture retention in rain-fed sorghum plots on a sandy Sahelian soil

headings.text: Biochar amendment and soil moisture retention in rain-fed sorghum plots on a sandy Sahelian soil

key_sentences: Sandy soils of the Sahel hold little water, and rain-fed crops often suffer from dry spells within the growing season.
The results suggest that biochar is most useful when it is combined with a nutrient source.

The objectives of this study were to quantify the effect of two biochar rates on volumetric soil water content during the rainy season, and to compare the grain yield of sorghum under biochar, manure and their combination.
Five treatments were arranged in a randomised complete block design with four replicates, on plots of 6 m by 8 m.
Grain yield was analysed by one-way analysis of variance, and differences between treatments were declared significant at P < 0.05.
Both biochar rates increased water content in the topsoil compared with the control, and the effect persisted throughout the season.
The combined treatment shows that the two amendments are complementary: manure supplies nutrients, while biochar helps the crop to bridge short dry spells.
Its effect on sorghum yield was large only when it was combined with manure.
